svg.text: The city's cars: sedan, van, bus, bike, and a wreck
Faceted side-on silhouettes in the city's own paints, each whole and wrecked; scenery, and something a fighter can throw. Concept art, working labels, pending Legal; city art, so it may be public.
Whole and wrecked (0.74 pixels to a unit; the bar on the left is a fighter, 75 units)
The paints (the city tints' walls; the nearest lane colour is far in every case)
Thrown: the tumble at fight size (86 px a fighter) and at 46 px, with a flat fighter for scale

Sizes are real-world lengths at the game's scale (a fighter is 75 units, about 1.75 m): the sedan 193 by 62, the van 223 by 86, the bus 516 by 137, the bike 90 by 56. Wheels are octagons (radius 14, 17, 22, 15). Each car is about 10
rigid parts: body, cabin, glass, two wheels, lights, a sill band; the bus 14; the bike 8. About 120, 150, 260 and 90 triangles (estimates).

Paints: six, the walls of the city's tints (low chroma, in the same family as the buildings, so a street of cars reads as part of the city and never as a fighter); the glass is the tint's dark glass; the lights are the city's one

lit colour, small and steady, and go dark in the wreck. Nothing is orange or yellow (a taxi would be fire's colour), mid blue (the sea's) or a saturated red (blood's). The lane colours are far from every paint except the training
dummy's pale lavender-grey ring, which sits near a light grey car: the dummy is told apart by his keyline.

The wreck: the same silhouette made lower and askew (the roof crushed by about a quarter, the body tilted 6 to 9 degrees, one wheel off or sprung, the bike's front wheel off), the glass out and soot-dark, the lights dark, a soot
band along the roof and the sill. No flame or smoke in the art, and no people in or around a car. A thrown car that lands becomes the wreck.

For Combat: Art suggests mass classes (bike 1, sedan 3, van 4, bus 8) and the first tier that can throw each (tier 1 the bike, 2 the sedan, 3 the van, 4 the bus), with the hit box the car's own size; these are suggestions in
